formation.locator: Berkelman, chapter 2 (Program Advisory Committee of 15 February 1978)
formation.note: Date the PAC selected the Columbia-Stony Brook proposal; used as a lower bound for the collaboration formation.
formation.quote: The winning entry was the sodium iodide and lead-glass array proposed by the group from Columbia and Stony Brook with Leon Lederman as spokesman.

intervals.label: CESR data taking (north area)
intervals.locator: Berkelman, chapter 10 (The CLEO-2 Years); "since the turn-on of CESR in 1979" (chapter 5)
intervals.note: Start: CUSB had run "since the turn-on of CESR in 1979"; the month is taken from the first colliding-beam luminosity on 14 August 1979 (chapter 3); end derived as 1979 + eleven years (the PAC terminated CUSB after one more Υ(4S) run in the early CLEO-2 era). CUSB-II (BGO upgrade) was chosen by the PAC in January 1984.
intervals.quote: CUSB under the leadership of the Franzinis had run in the north interaction region for eleven years

intervals.label: CUSB terminated
intervals.note: Year derived (see the active interval); the detector was dismantled afterwards.
intervals.quote: Upon the advice of the PAC I decided to terminate the CUSB experiment after one more run on the Υ(4S).

summary.plain: The Columbia University and Stony Brook collaboration, led first by Leon Lederman and then by Paolo and Juliet Franzini, that built CUSB. Later members included Louisiana State University and the Max Planck Institute in Munich.
summary.technical: CUSB collaboration: Columbia and Stony Brook (spokesman L. Lederman, then P. and J. Franzini), joined by LSU (muon detector) and MPI Munich (small-angle NaI arrays) by 1983; after CUSB the experimenters moved to DØ at Fermilab and the Franzinis later set up KLOE at Frascati (Berkelman).
